To determine the physical dimension of molar energy, we start with its definition: molar energy is energy divided by the amount of substance.

1.  **Dimension of Energy (E):**
    Energy has the same dimensions as work. Work is defined as force multiplied by distance:
    $$\text{Work} = \text{Force} \times \text{Length}$$
    Force is defined as mass multiplied by acceleration:
    $$\text{Force} = \text{Mass} \times \text{Acceleration}$$
    Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity over time:
    $$\text{Acceleration} = \frac{\text{Length}}{\text{Time}^2}$$
    Substituting these back, we get:
    $$\text{Energy} = (\text{Mass} \times \frac{\text{Length}}{\text{Time}^2}) \times \text{Length} = \frac{\text{Mass} \times \text{Length}^2}{\text{Time}^2}$$

2.  **Dimension of Amount (n):**
    The amount of substance is a base dimension, denoted as **Amount**.

3.  **Dimension of Molar Energy:**
    Molar energy is the ratio of energy to the amount of substance:
    $$\text{Molar Energy} = \frac{\text{Energy}}{\text{Amount}}$$
    Substituting the dimensions for energy and amount:
    $$\text{Molar Energy} = \frac{\text{Mass} \times \text{Length}^2 / \text{Time}^2}{\text{Amount}} = \frac{\text{Mass} \times \text{Length}^2}{\text{Time}^2 \times \text{Amount}}$$

Using the requested format (product of base dimensions using *, /, and ^):
<ANSWER>Mass * Length^2 / (Time^2 * Amount)</ANSWER>
